blocks.orig: In Tanzania, mountains are a common sight. In fact, they’re arguably one of the riches that this country is famous for. If you’re interested in hiking or mountain climbing, it can be difficult to decide which of the mountains in Tanzania you are most interested in.
blocks.html: Mountains are everywhere in Tanzania; you could even say they are among the treasures the country is known for. For anyone keen on hiking or mountaineering, choosing which of Tanzania’s mountains appeals most can be a tough call.

blocks.orig: Let’s explore some of the tallest mountains in Tanzania and the hikes they have to offer.
blocks.html: Below we look at some of the highest mountains in Tanzania and the hikes you can do on them.

blocks.orig: Most Prominent Mountains of Tanzania By Height
blocks.html: Tanzania’s main mountains ranked by height

blocks.orig: With so many mountains in Tanzania, it can be difficult to keep track of them all. Of course, everyone is familiar with Mount Kilimanjaro.
blocks.html: Tanzania has so many mountains that keeping track of them all is no easy task. Mount Kilimanjaro, of course, needs no introduction.

blocks.orig: However, in Tanzania, there are mountains that don’t enjoy anywhere near as much notoriety. That doesn’t mean that they’re not noteworthy or don’t have anything to offer the intrepid hiker.
blocks.html: Yet the country also has mountains that are far less well known. That does not make them any less worthwhile, nor does it mean they have nothing to give the adventurous hiker.

blocks.orig: While not all of these peaks may offer the same challenge to mountain climbers and mountaineers, that doesn’t mean that each peak doesn’t have something unique to offer. Let’s have a closer look at some of what these mountains have to offer.
blocks.html: Not every one of these peaks presents the same challenge to climbers and mountaineers, but each of them has something of its own to give. Here is a closer look at what some of these mountains hold in store.

blocks.orig: Mount Kilimanjaro: The Highest Mountain in Africa
blocks.html: Mount Kilimanjaro: Africa’s highest mountain

blocks.orig: Mount Kilimanjaro is the most famous mountain of Tanzania, by far. Not only is it the highest mountain in Tanzania, it’s also the highest mountain in Africa. At 5,895 metres (19,340 feet), Mount Kilimanjaro is also the world’s highest freestanding mountain above sea level.
blocks.html: By a wide margin, Mount Kilimanjaro is Tanzania’s best-known mountain. It is the highest peak not only in Tanzania but in the whole of Africa, and at 5,895 metres (19,340 feet) it is also the highest freestanding mountain above sea level anywhere in the world.

blocks.orig: For all of these reasons, Mount Kilimanjaro is a popular tourist destination, and people climb it regularly. However, there’s more to this mountain than the chance to climb to the top. Some other activities you can experience on and around this majestic peak include the following:
blocks.html: All of this makes Mount Kilimanjaro a popular destination, and it is climbed regularly. But the mountain offers more than just a summit attempt. Other things you can do on and around this majestic peak include:

blocks.orig: The Rundugai Hotsprings – If you just want to take a breather and relax, the Rundugai Hotsprings are ideal. Explore the crystal clear waters while the natural heat draws all the tension from your muscles.
blocks.html: Rundugai Hotsprings – Looking for nothing more than a pause and some relaxation? Then the Rundugai Hotsprings are perfect. Wade into the crystal clear water and let the natural warmth ease every bit of tension from your muscles.

blocks.orig: Hiking to the Kilimanjaro Waterfall – The Kilimanjaro waterfall is a lovely cascade of water, and hiking to it and back is an excellent day trip. The trail is less steeply inclined than the one to Mount Meru’s waterfall, and even beginners can take the trip with ease.
blocks.html: Walk to the Kilimanjaro Waterfall – This lovely cascade makes a fine day trip when you hike there and back. The path climbs less steeply than the trail to Mount Meru’s waterfall, so even beginners can manage it comfortably.

blocks.orig: Hiking on Kilimanjaro – If you’d like to experience the beauty and splendour of the peak but don’t necessarily want to climb all the way to the summit, why not try hiking on the mountain instead? You can go for a one-day hike or choose for a two-day hike and sleep on the mountain and experience the beauty and serenity without the strain of a full climb.
blocks.html: A hike on Kilimanjaro – Keen to take in the beauty and grandeur of the peak without going all the way to the top? Then a hike on the mountain is a good alternative. Choose a one-day walk, or opt for a two-day hike with a night on the mountain, and enjoy the scenery and calm without the effort of a full ascent.

blocks.orig: This mountain truly has a lot more to offer than people think, and the options are endless.
blocks.html: There is far more to this mountain than most people realise, and the possibilities go on and on.

blocks.orig: Mount Mawenzi, is a peak of the Kilimanjaro, the second-highest peak in Tanzania after Uhuru Peak. There are plenty of things you can do around this peak. There are three different hiking routes on this mountain, with varying levels of difficulty:
blocks.html: Mount Mawenzi is one of Kilimanjaro’s peaks and, after Uhuru Peak, the second-highest in Tanzania. The area around it offers plenty to do, and the mountain itself has three different hiking routes of varying difficulty:

blocks.orig: All in all, hiking this mountain is relatively easy, and you should reach the summit on the same day that you start the hike. This gives you a fantastic opportunity to take photos and enjoy the view before heading back.
blocks.html: On the whole, this is a fairly easy mountain to hike, and you can expect to stand on the summit the same day you set off. That leaves you with a great chance to take pictures and soak up the view before you head down again.

blocks.orig: As the third-highest mountain in Tanzania, Mount Meru enjoys some popularity among tourists. Hiking or climbing it is much less demanding than taking on Kilimanjaro itself and still gives you the opportunity to enjoy stunning vistas and a wonderful hike.
blocks.html: Mount Meru, Tanzania’s third-highest mountain, is fairly popular with visitors. Walking or climbing it demands far less than tackling Kilimanjaro, while still rewarding you with stunning views and a wonderful hike.

blocks.orig: Another great aspect of Mount Meru is that it has its very own waterfall. If you take the trek to the Mount Meru Waterfall, you’ll discover stunning views after a comparatively short hike. Enjoy the beauty and tranquillity of the waterfall without the strain involved in visiting some other falls.
blocks.html: Another plus of Mount Meru is its very own waterfall. Take the trek to the Mount Meru Waterfall and a relatively short walk brings you to stunning views. You get to enjoy the beauty and quiet of the falls without the exertion that some other waterfalls demand.

blocks.orig: Klute Peak is one of the peaks belonging to Shira Mountain and, thus, to Mount Kilimanjaro. Generally, it is not used as a stand-alone hike or climb. Instead, it forms part of some routes leading to Kilimanjaro’s summit.
blocks.html: Klute Peak belongs to Shira Mountain and therefore to Mount Kilimanjaro. It is rarely hiked or climbed on its own; rather, it lies on some of the routes that lead to Kilimanjaro’s summit.

blocks.orig: Mount Hanang is the fifth-highest of Tanzania’s mountain peaks. It may not be the most recognizable among the mountains of Tanzania, but it’s still beautiful. As with Mount Mawenzi, there are three main established hiking trails to get to the summit.
blocks.html: Fifth among Tanzania’s peaks is Mount Hanang. It is not the most familiar of the country’s mountains, yet it is beautiful all the same. Like Mount Mawenzi, it has three main established trails leading to the summit.

blocks.orig: You can choose between the Giting Route, the Ngendabi Route, and the Katesh Route.
blocks.html: The options are the Giting Route, the Ngendabi Route and the Katesh Route.

blocks.orig: The Katesh Route has an ascension time of around six hours and a decent time of around five. The Giting and Ngendabi Routes should take similar amounts of time. However, the details of each route may vary significantly.
blocks.html: On the Katesh Route the climb takes around six hours and the descent around five. The Giting and Ngendabi Routes take roughly as long, although the specifics of each route can differ considerably.

blocks.orig: You can hike Luhombero Peak from the park’s outskirts and turn it into a full expedition. Walking safaris are an option and will allow you to experience more of the scenery and local wildlife. However, this will also turn a one or two-day hike into a five or six-day hike.
blocks.html: Luhombero Peak can be hiked from the edge of the park and made into a proper expedition. Walking safaris are possible too and let you see more of the landscape and local wildlife, though they stretch a one or two-day hike into a five or six-day one.

blocks.orig: You can choose between several routes that have drastically different travel times. For instance, you can decide to take a circular route that will have you hiking around the mountain. You can also pick a more direct route and shorten the time spent significantly.
blocks.html: Several routes are available, and their durations differ a great deal. You might take a circular route that leads you all the way around the mountain, or go for a more direct one and cut the time needed considerably.

blocks.orig: Whichever route you decide to take, this mountain is well worth the effort and will reward you with a range of intriguing experiences and stunning vistas.
blocks.html: Whatever route you settle on, the mountain repays the effort with a variety of intriguing experiences and stunning views.

blocks.orig: Tanzania has a total of 2,395 notable peaks and hills that have been named. That’s not to say that there are only that many peaks. Many smaller or less noteworthy peaks simply haven’t been named. As you might expect, there are many other Tanzanian mountains that are well worth mentioning. Let’s have a closer look at a few of them.
blocks.html: In total, 2,395 notable peaks and hills in Tanzania have been given names. That does not mean there are only that many; plenty of smaller or less remarkable peaks have simply never been named. As you would expect, many other Tanzanian mountains deserve a mention, so here are a few of them.

blocks.orig: Mount Ol Doinyo Lengai is known to the local Tanzanian people—the Maasai—as ‘The Mountain of God.’ They believe that the god Engai made his home there after a hunter successfully hit him with an arrow.
blocks.html: To the local Maasai, Mount Ol Doinyo Lengai is ‘The Mountain of God.’ According to their belief, the god Engai settled there after a hunter managed to strike him with an arrow.

blocks.orig: The mountain is an active volcano that last had an explosive eruption in 1993. It has two craters, one of which is typically active, while the other is filled with water.
blocks.html: It is an active volcano whose last explosive eruption was in 1993. There are two craters: one is usually active, the other holds water.

blocks.orig: If you’re fit and looking for a challenge, then this mountain in Tanzania is well worth considering. It’s often considered one of the most challenging nighttime mountain hikes. Located in Ngorongoro Conservation area, it’s quite a journey to get there because it’s far from basically everything, but it’s an amazing hike you would want to go for.
blocks.html: For fit hikers after a real challenge, this Tanzanian mountain deserves serious thought. It is widely regarded as one of the toughest night-time mountain hikes. It lies in the Ngorongoro Conservation area, and getting there is quite a trip, as it’s a long way from just about everything, but it’s an amazing hike that’s worth going for.

blocks.orig: The Olmoti Crater is considered one of the better hikes for beginners. It offers a less strenuous hike than some other options without decreasing the value of the hike.
blocks.html: The Olmoti Crater counts as one of the better walks for beginners. It is less strenuous than some of the other options, yet no less rewarding.

blocks.orig: Hiking the Olmoti Crater only takes around 40 minutes and goes through an ancient caldera. You’ll be able to enjoy beautiful panoramic views as well as experience the glory of the Munge waterfall.
blocks.html: The walk up the Olmoti Crater takes just around 40 minutes and leads through an ancient caldera. Along the way you get beautiful panoramic views and the splendour of the Munge waterfall.

blocks.orig: Olmoti means cooking pot in the language of the Masai and refers to the large, pot-like shape of the caldera.
blocks.html: In the Masai language, Olmoti means cooking pot, a reference to the caldera’s big, pot-like shape.

blocks.orig: This hike is only about 3 kilometres (1.9 miles) long, but bear in mind that it climbs by about 304 metres (1,000 feet), so the altitude can be gruelling.
blocks.html: The route is only about 3 kilometres (1.9 miles) long, but keep in mind that it gains about 304 metres (1,000 feet), so the altitude can make it hard going.

blocks.orig: If you want to explore the glory and majesty of Kilimanjaro but don’t necessarily want to climb the whole peak or spend a few days hiking, there is an alternative option.
blocks.html: Would you like to take in the grandeur of Kilimanjaro without climbing the whole mountain or spending several days on foot? There is another way.

blocks.orig: What’s a better way to experience Africa’s highest mountain than from a plane? This 45-minute flight allows you to see Kilimanjaro as you never have before.
blocks.html: Is there a finer way to see Africa’s highest mountain than from the air? On this 45-minute flight you see Kilimanjaro from a completely new angle.

blocks.orig: Enjoy the sight of the crater and all the cascading glaciers as you swoop overhead and view aspects of the mountain you’d never see from the ground.
blocks.html: As you pass overhead you take in the crater and the cascading glaciers, and see sides of the mountain that stay hidden from the ground.

blocks.orig: Each tour has a requisite number of people before the flight can take off. To successfully enjoy the tour, the flight must have at least four passengers on board.
blocks.html: A minimum number of participants is needed before any flight can depart: at least four passengers must be on board for the tour to go ahead.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is a beautiful country with many natural wonders, beautiful sites, and lovely hiking trails. It also has an array of mountains and hills.
blocks.html: Tanzania is a beautiful country full of natural wonders, lovely places and fine hiking trails, with a wide range of mountains and hills on top.

blocks.orig: The mountains of Tanzania are wondrous, majestic, and full of hidden jewels. From climbing to the summit of Kilimanjaro to trekking the lower slopes of Mount Sisaba, there’s always something new to find and do.
blocks.html: Majestic and full of hidden gems, the mountains of Tanzania always offer something new to discover, whether you climb to the summit of Kilimanjaro or trek the lower slopes of Mount Sisaba.
